title: Why machines will still not rule the world
abstract: arXiv:2610.11424v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In our book Why machines will never rule the world [13, 14] we argue that arti- ficial general intelligence is mathematically impossible. This is because the human beings and the processes which exhibit intelligence are complex systems whose be- haviour cannot be captured by the kinds of models that we can generate with or without computers. Proponents of contemporary machine intelligence respond with two lines of argument: a theoretical one, grounded in the universal approximation theorems for neural networks and the Church-Turing-Deutsch principle; and an em- pirical one, grounded in rapidly rising scores on standardized benchmarks. In this communication we examine and reject both responses. First, we show serious issues in the physicalist counter-argument based on the Church-Turing-Deutsch principle. translated_title: 为什么机器仍然不会统治世界
translated_abstract: 在我们的著作《为什么机器永远不会统治世界》[13, 14]中，我们论证了人工通用智能在数学上是不可能的。这是因为人类以及展现智能的过程属于复杂系统，其行为无法被我们借助或不借助计算机所能生成的模型所捕捉。当代机器智能的支持者以两条论证路线作出回应：一条是理论性的，立足于神经网络的全局逼近定理和丘奇-图灵-多伊奇原理；另一条是经验性的，立足于标准化基准测试中快速攀升的分数。在这篇通讯中，我们检验并驳斥了这两种回应。首先，我们指出了基于丘奇-图灵-多伊奇原理的物理主义反驳论证中的严重问题。其次，我们回顾了近期的证据，表明一些著名的基准测试已受到训练数据污染和有缺陷的测试方法的影响而失去可靠性。
tldr: 本文通过驳斥基于丘奇-图灵-多伊奇原理的理论论证和因训练数据污染而失效的基准测试经验论证，坚持了人工通用智能在数学上不可能实现的论断。
en_tdlr: By refuting both the theoretical argument based on the Church-Turing-Deutsch principle and the empirical benchmark evidence compromised by training-data contamination, this paper maintains its claim that artificial general intelligence is mathematically impossible.
